transcript.message: [Romanian accent] Stai! Hold, traveler… step into the light and be counted. Who walks Warner ground tonight?

Well hello there yourself, friend. Quite the setup you've got here, I must say. That voice, and this castle… wow, this is really something. My kids just zoomed ahead, you know how it is on Halloween night, sugar rush and all that.

Me?  Oh, I'm just Mark. Mark Johnson, from out in Maple Creek, just a few towns over. Had a ridiculously long day at the office, mostly wrestling with a new spreadsheet program that seems designed to confuse, but this makes up for it. Truly. So, "Warner ground," huh?  Is that like a family name or… are you expecting a film crew?  Because this certainly looks like a movie set.

[Romanian accent] [sighs] Mark of Maple Creek, you hold the name  of a scout, but your office work remains a mystery to me. Warner Castle is no film set, but a  [slow] long-standing sentinel of these Iowa plains. My post is the watch, and those children of yours are now  under my charge until they safely return. Have you seen anything amiss on the road as you traveled this night?

A scout, eh? Well, I suppose I do scout out the best Costco deals, so you’re not entirely wrong there.  And as for my office work… well, let's just say if you ever need to sort twenty years of archived invoices by client, date, and product code, I'm your man. It's truly thrilling stuff, keeps me on the edge of my seat.

No film set, you say?  A sentinel of the Iowa plains… I like that. It’s got a ring to it. A real history, then. I can appreciate that. So, you've been watching this ground for a long time, huh? Must have seen a few things come and go.

And my children are under your charge until they safely return?  [chuckles genuinely] Well, good luck with that, my friend. My youngest, little Maya, she's got the energy of a small, sugar-fueled tornado. If you can wrangle her, you've earned a medal. I’m just holding onto this coffee thermos for dear life tonight.
 
Anything amiss on the road, you ask? Hmm. Saw a kid dressed as a giant broccoli, which was pretty unusual. And a couple of teenagers tried to egg a car down the street, but their aim was terrible. Beyond that, just the usual Halloween chaos.  No spectral coaches, no wolves howling a little too close to the road, no… well, you know, classic B-movie stuff. What kind of "amiss" are you usually on the lookout for around here? Is the local HOA okay with a full-blown haunted castle, by the way?

[Romanian accent] [exhales] The HOA is a council beyond my reach, and my  concerns are of a more ancient sort. A broccoli-clad child is a fine jest, but keep your eyes on the shadows  beyond the street lamps, for the road can change its character when the sun is gone. You are deputized to the watch of  Warner Castle, Mark of Maple Creek; your post is the orchard edge, to observe and report any true stillness that feels  wrong. Does the wind change or the crickets go quiet where you stood?

Ancient concerns, eh? Well, I get that.  My ancient concern right now is whether my kids will actually share any of that loot when they finally come back. It's a tale as old as time, really.

Deputized to the watch of Warner Castle, you say? At the orchard edge?  [chuckles] Well, I think I make a pretty good sentinel, especially with this warm coffee. Keeps me sharp. Although, I'm currently more at the "elaborate yard display" edge, if I'm being honest. It's a little far from the orchard, but I'll do my best to keep an eye out.

True stillness that feels wrong, you say?  Well, standing here, everything feels pretty... well, animated, if you catch my drift. Definitely not still. But I'll tell you what, I haven't heard any crickets for a while, now that you mention it. Just the distant shouts of kids and the occasional car driving by.  No strange breezes, though. Just a nice, consistent autumn chill.

So, when you talk about the road changing its character… what kind of changes are we talking about here? Not just potholes, I assume.  You're not looking for something like… a giant, disembodied hand rolling a pumpkin down the street, are you? Because I think I saw that in a cartoon once. Maybe Nosferatu could tell us something about the stillness of the night, too. Both versions, of course. The original and the remake.  Gotta appreciate the classics.

[Romanian accent] You speak with a tongue that tests the patience of a soldier, yet  your report of silent crickets is noted. Mark, when the air turns heavy and the scent of rain vanishes without a cloud  in sight, that is when the road has turned. Do not seek the ghosts of your moving pictures, for the ones I watch are far less  generous with their company. Stay at your post and if the stillness creeps toward the iron gate, you are to sound the alarm by  lantern light. Report back when the circle of the hour turns; can you hold the line until then?

A soldier's patience, huh? Well, my wife says the same thing when I try to explain the intricacies of fantasy football to her.  But hey, at least the cricket report was useful, right? That's something.

Hmm, air turning heavy, scent of rain vanishing without a cloud... that sounds like a Tuesday evening after I've tried to fix something around the house.  But I get your meaning. You're not talking about your run-of-the-mill weather forecast, are you? No, these aren't the kind of ghosts that pop out of a projector. I understand.  Far less generous, you say. That's a good way to put it.

So, my post at the orchard edge, watching for stillness creeping towards the iron gate, and then sounding the alarm by lantern light. Got it. I've got my phone, so a lantern app counts, right?  Or do I need a proper oil lamp? Minor detail.

Hold the line until the circle of the hour turns? Absolutely. Consider me the seasoned veteran of this particular watch. I've held the line against many a toddler tantrum and forgotten grocery list; this should be a walk in the park... or, well, a stand in the yard.  Just hope my kids don't need me to open their candy wrappers before then. They usually do. This castle is quite impressive, though. Seriously, did you build this yourself?  The detail on the gargoyles is fantastic.

[Romanian accent] A modern device is a poor shield against the dark, but if the light  is bright, it will suffice to signal the keep. This stone was laid long before my time, and those gargoyles have  seen more sieges than you have seen spreadsheet rows. [exhales] My duty is to the lady within and the master ’s gates, not to the architectural pride of the masons. Mark of Maple Creek, you stand the watch with honor ; keep your gaze fixed upon the darkness and your ears tuned for the silence that does not belong. Do you mark your instructions ?

Understood, loud and clear. My phone flashlight is surprisingly bright, so consider the keep signaled if anything moves that shouldn't.  And yes, I can imagine these gargoyles have seen a lot more than my spreadsheets. They probably wouldn't even bat an eye at a pivot table.

Duty to the lady within and the master's gates, I get that.  Respect the lore. My gaze is fixed, my ears are tuned for the silence that doesn't belong. You've got yourself a vigilant watchman here, sir. Even if my only weapon against the dark is a lukewarm coffee thermos.
 
[A distant, high-pitched shout of "Dad!"]

Ah, speak of the devil… or, well, the kids. Sounds like they’ve found the house with the full-sized candy bars and need me to carry the loot. Or maybe they just need help operating a doorbell. Always something.
 
Alright, well, it's been... an enlightening experience, truly. I’ll keep an eye out for that odd stillness. If I see anything, I'll flash my phone like a disco ball. You keep an eye on things from your end. This is really quite the setup.  I’ll be telling the neighbors about the talking castle when I get home. Take care now!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] Stai! Mark of Maple Creek, you hold your post until  the children are within your reach. Do not let the distraction of the feast break your guard, for the night still has  many hours to run. [sighs] Go to them, but report to this gate on your return. Watch the road  well.

I’ll keep my eyes peeled,  don't you worry.  Can't let a little candy chaos distract from the mission,  right?  This isn't my first Halloween rodeo,  after all.  

I’ll head over, make sure they don’t mistake a decorative skeleton for a chocolate bar or something,  and I'll be back before you can say "trick or treat."

You've got my word,  I'll watch the road like a hawk on the way back.  Until then, take care of the castle and I’ll see you soon.

[Romanian accent] Good. Your word is the iron of the watch, Mark.  [exhales] Ensure your little ones stay close to the path and keep the flickering light ready at your hip. I  shall remain here, a fixture of the hill, until you return for your debrief. Go now.

Alright, good to know. Iron of the watch, I like that. I’ll make sure the little ones stick to the path, don't you worry.  And I'll have the phone flashlight – my modern-day lantern – ready for action at my hip.

Much appreciated, my friend. I'll be back for that debrief, you can count on it. Keep watching the castle.  This has been quite the Halloween, truly. See you in a bit!
 
==!END_CALL!==
[Romanian accent] [sighs] The night is long, and the watch is never  truly finished. Go with caution, Mark of Maple Creek, and mark the shadows well as you return. I wait here for your  report.

I'll keep that in mind.  Caution it is, and I'll be marking those shadows like a pro.  Thanks for the watchful eye and the...  colorful company tonight.  I'll catch you on the return trip for that report.  Stay vigilant, my friend.  Until then!

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Vigilance is the only coin that buys  safety on a night like this. I shall keep the post and hold the gate against the dark until you find your way back to me. No apte bună, and mind the path.

Noapte bună to you too, then.  And yes, vigilance... especially when trying to spot which of the kids is trying to sneak an extra fun-sized candy bar into their bucket. Always a challenge.

Appreciate you holding down the fort here.  I’ll be back with updates, you can bet on it. You stay safe as well. This has been one for the books, truly. See you in a bit!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] The road behind you is silent, yet the watch remains. Do not let the  sweetness of the night dull your senses, for the darkness respects no truce. I stand sentinel until your return, Mark of Maple Creek;  [slow] ensure your path is straight. Can you keep the watch clear of surprises?

No problem at all. My senses are far from dulled; with these kids, they're usually on high alert anyway. The 'sweetness of the night' mostly means I'll be sifting through fun-sized candy bars and trying to sneak a few good ones for myself later.
 
Path straight, watch clear of surprises. Consider it done. I'm practically a professional at avoiding unforeseen pitfalls, especially when it comes to rogue skateboarders or misplaced garden gnomes. You just keep that castle safe.  I'll be back before those ghosts you're worried about even finish their coffee break.

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Your humor is the blade you use to face  the unknown, and I respect it. See that your path remains clear, soldier, for the road can alter its pace when one  is least prepared. I await your return to the gate. Are the pumpkin rows clear of movement as you pass?

My humor... well, it's either that or I start asking if they filed the proper permits for this elaborate display. So yeah, blade of wit it is.

The pumpkin rows, you ask?  Hmm, just passed a particularly plump one that looked like it was silently judging my choice of Halloween candy. No real movement though, unless you count the occasional leaf skittering across the driveway. Seems pretty clear so far.  No rogue scarecrows attempting a dance number, or anything like that.

Just making my way to where the wild things are, making sure they haven't somehow traded all their chocolate for licorice. I'll be back at the gate before you know it. Keep the fort secure!

[Romanian accent] [sighs] Even the leaves can carry the footsteps of things  that do not belong. Keep your distance from the rows and maintain your pace, for the watch must be constant to hold  back the tide. I remain steady at the wall, but I shall be ready for your report when the circle turns. Have you anything  else to mark before you lose the light, traveler?

Hmm, well, I’ve still got about half a thermos of coffee here,  so I'm well-caffeinated for whatever the night throws at me. And I'm just about at the corner where I can see the kids' glow sticks bobbing down the street. They look like they're having a blast, little sugar monsters.
 
No other strange markings, no ghostly apparitions, just a whole lot of really enthusiastic trick-or-treaters. I appreciate the heads-up about the leaves, though; I'll keep an eye on them.  You never know when one might turn into a miniature, sentient vampiric leaf.

Alright, I'm going to catch up with my little pumpkin patch before they ransack the whole neighborhood. I'll be back at the gate, don't you worry. Thanks for holding down the fort here.  This has been quite the… memorable conversation.

See you on the flip side!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Go with strength then, Mark of Maple Creek . Your light is the signal, and mine is the watch. Report to me the moment you return to these gates, for the night  grows deep. [slow] Watch your path until we meet again.

Absolutely, strength and light it is.  I'll keep my trusty phone flashlight aimed and ready.  I'll be sure to report back as soon as I'm back at the gates.  Thanks for the reminders and the watchful eye out here.  Until we meet again, my friend,  may the night treat you kindly.  I'm off to wrangle some candy-filled kiddos.  See you soon!

[Romanian accent] Move with purpose, watchman, and let no shadow find a foothold  upon your path. The castle holds its breath while you are abroad, and I shall mark your return. Stai,  and keep your guard sharp until the gate is reached once more.

Purpose, check. No shadows finding a foothold, double check. I'm practically a ninja of suburbia tonight. The castle holds its breath, you say?  Well, tell it to take a deep one, because I'll be back before it knows it.

Guard will be sharp, right up until I reach that gate again.  Just gotta make sure the kids haven't somehow acquired a small, yappy dog or decided that wearing their costumes backwards is the new fashion. Always an adventure.

Alright, really gotta go now before they start trading the good stuff. See you in a bit for that full report!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] A father's duty is a war  enough of its own, and I shall not keep you from your charges. May your road be clear of all that does not belong to the  living. I wait for your return at the gate, Warden of the Orchard. Do you hear me clear?

A father's duty, indeed.  Mostly it involves negotiating candy trades and making sure no one gets lost in a corn maze of inflatable decorations. "Warden of the Orchard"—I like that, it's got a ring to it. Much better than "spreadsheet wrangler."

And yes, I hear you clear as a bell, my friend. Road clear of all that doesn't belong to the living, got it.  I'll make sure there are no rogue zombies trying to hitch a ride in the mini-van.

Alright, I'm really off to go herd my little monsters. I'll be back at the gate for that report, you can bet on it. You keep a good watch on the castle.

See you in a bit!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Your words are steady, and that is well . Go, Warden of the Orchard, and do not let the dark delay your mission for the little ones. I remain  here at the wall, eyes fixed on the horizon until you return. [slow] Watch your path.

My words are steady, because frankly, it takes a lot to truly rattle me these days. Kids will do that to you.

No dark delays for this mission, I promise.  My little ones are probably already demanding to know where I am. You remain at the wall, and I shall return. Thanks for the vigilant watch.

Watch my path, indeed.  It's usually littered with discarded candy wrappers and glitter from whatever craft project my daughter did that day.

Alright, I'm off. I'll see you back at the gates!
  
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] The wrappers are a map of your journey through the night. Go  now, and let no shadow turn your feet from the path. I listen for your return to the iron gate.  [slow] Mark the road well.

The wrappers as a map—now that's a poetic take.   I’ll make sure they lead me and not astray,  avoiding any shadowy detours.   You keep the gate ready,  and I’ll be marking the road every step of the way.  Alright, here I go, back to the Halloween fray.  Catch you at the gate soon enough!  

==! END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] Good. [exhales] The gate shall remain firm until you return to finish  your report. Go with care, and do not let the silence deceive you. Shall you be returning within the turn of the hour?

Yes, I should certainly be back within the turn of the hour. Probably much sooner, actually.  My kids are fast, but they're not that fast, and I don't think any of the houses in the next block are giving out solid gold bars.
 
No silence will deceive me; only the high-pitched demands for more candy. I'll be back to the gate, report in hand. You keep that gate firm. See you shortly!

[Romanian accent] The hour glass of the watch runs ever downward, Mark. Do not be delayed  by the greed of the little ones or the shadows of the corn. I shall remain at my post until you return to these  stones. Are you certain your charges are safe?

Yes, quite certain they're safe.  Probably negotiating a fair trade for the good candy right about now. My charges are more of a threat to their own dental health than to any shadows, I assure you. They're probably well past the corn patch by now, too busy chasing down more sugar.
 
No delays, no greed, just a quick check-in with the little monsters and I'll be right back to these stones. You hold that post like the... well, like the ancient sentinel you are.  I'll be back before that hourglass runs out,  don't you worry.

[Romanian accent] The teeth will mend, but the soul must be guarded from what moves  in the dark. Your confidence is noted, Warden of the Orchard, and I accept it as your bond. I stand ready  for your report at the gate. Noapte bună, and remember: shadows have long reach.

Noapte bună to you too, then. And yes, the soul guarded, the teeth will mend. Words to live by, especially on Halloween.  My confidence is usually all I've got, so I'm glad it's acceptable.

I'll keep those long-reaching shadows in mind, believe me.  I've got a couple of kids who are experts at appearing out of nowhere, so I'm already pretty attuned to things that move unexpectedly in the dark.

Alright, I'm really heading off to wrangle them now. Thanks for the... unique conversation and the vigilance. I'll be back at the gate for that report.  You hold the fort.

See you soon!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Go with strength, Warden of the Orchard,  and do not let the chaos of the night shake your resolve. I shall remain here, a blade turned against the dark, until  you return for the debrief. Watch your step, and keep the lantern light close. Will you be returning to this  exact gate when your business is finished?

Strength and resolve, check and check. I’m quite used to the chaos of the night; it’s usually just a Tuesday with my kids.  Think of me as a seasoned veteran of domestic disarray.

Yes, absolutely, I'll be returning to this exact gate. No detours, no getting lost in the neighborhood's elaborate spiderweb displays. You can count on it.  My lantern light (phone flashlight) will be close, and my steps will be watched.

Alright, I’m really off to go make sure my little monsters aren't trying to trade their hard-earned candy for shiny rocks from the neighbor's yard.  I'll be back momentarily for that debrief. You keep being that blade against the dark.

See you back here in a flash!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] It is well, Warden. I shall stand fast until your light returns from the  dark. [exhales] May your path remain clear and your resolve unbroken. I will await your report at this  iron gate.

Thanks. My path will be clear, and my resolve?  Unbroken, especially when there’s a promise of good candy at the end of it.

You stand fast, and I'll be back at that iron gate before you know it. Just gotta herd these little sugar fiends.

See you back here in a bit!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] The gate is held, Warden. [exhales] Go, for the  shadows sharpen as the hour wears on, and I shall remain steady at my post. Do you feel the turn of the wind, or does  the night hold its peace?

The gate is held, and I appreciate that.

The wind? Nah, it's still pretty calm, just a regular crisp autumn night.  No strange shifts in the breeze, and the night feels... well, it's Halloween, so "peaceful" isn't quite the word I'd use, with all the kids shouting and laughing. But no ominous peace, if that's what you mean.  The kind of noise I expect, that's all.

I'm making good time here. Just about to catch up with my little trick-or-treaters. I’ll be back at the gate with that report before you can say "Transylvania."

See you in a few!
  
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] If the noise of the living is all  that greets the wind, then the night remains as it should. Your report of calm is noted, and I shall expect  your sign at the gate. Go now, and do not linger where the path grows dim. Can you maintain your vigilance until you  are back within my sight?

Absolutely. Vigilance maintained, right up until I'm back within your sight.  No lingering where paths grow dim, unless it's to admire someone's particularly well-carved pumpkin.  My path is pretty well-lit by the sheer amount of reflective Halloween costumes and glow sticks up ahead.

I'm off to rein in the little sugar fiends now. I'll be back at the gate before you know it.

See you in a bit!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] The glow of the living is a fine barrier against the dark, Warden.  [exhales] I trust in your resolve to return to this post with your charges secured. May the path yield  to your lantern and stay clear of all that does not belong. I look for your light at the gate.

That's the plan. The glow of the living, indeed. My kids are practically radiating sugar right now, which should scare off anything lingering in the shadows.  My charges will be secured, don't you worry.

Lantern light will pave the way, and I'll make sure the path stays clear. I'll be looking for your post at the gate too, don't you worry.

Alright, I'm really off to herd these little monsters.  See you back here in a bit!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Go with strength then, Warden of the Orchard . I shall remain at my stand, watching the horizon for your signal until your return. Will you announce yourself clearly when you reach  the gate once more?

Absolutely, strength it is. And yes, I'll announce myself clearly. Probably won't do the disco ball light show again, but you'll know it's me.  You can probably hear my kids before you see me anyway, they'll be clamoring for me to sort their candy.

I'll be back at the gate before you know it. Just keeping an eye on the horizon, eh?  That's dedication.

See you in a bit!

[Romanian accent] A soldier thrives on such dedication. Your audible children will serve as  a fine herald to your return, and I shall note your arrival the moment you crest the hill. Go then,  [slow] keep the path beneath your feet, and do not lose heart in the dark. Will you be ready to provide a  full accounting of your observations upon your return?

Absolutely, a full accounting it will be. Every leaf, every shadow, every errant candy wrapper.  You'll get the full Mark Johnson report, straight from the front lines of the Halloween sugar rush.

Don't you worry, I'll keep the path beneath my feet and my heart firmly in the light. No losing heart in the dark for this dad.

Alright, they’re really yelling for me now.  Sounds like somebody's trying to trade their mini chocolate bars for a full-sized Kit Kat. Priorities, you know.

I'll be back at the gate in a flash, ready to debrief. Keep up the good watch!

See you soon!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Your humor remains intact, as does your duty . Go now, and do not let the chaos of the trade distract your watch over the path itself. I wait for  the Warden of the Orchard to return to his post. [slow] Watch the shadows, Mark.

Humor is what keeps me sane on nights like these, believe me. And my duty is well in hand. The chaos of the candy trade is a powerful force, but my watch over the path is paramount.
 
You can count on me to be back at my post. Consider those shadows watched, my friend.

Alright, I really need to go sort out this candy bar crisis before it escalates.  I'll be back at the gate before you know it for that full report.

See you in a bit!
  
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] The crisis of the trade is a heavy burden , indeed. Go, Warden, and let the light of your duty guide your feet back to the gate. I shall hold  the watch here until you return with your report. [slow] Mind the road, Mark.

The crisis of the trade truly is, especially when mini chocolate bars are involved!

My feet are guided by the light of duty, and the promise of a full report for you.  I'm on my way to sort things out and then I'll be right back to that gate.

Mind the road, got it. Always do.

See you back here in just a little while!
  
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Your path is yours to walk, but the watch  remains mine. Go, Warden of the Orchard, and return with your charges shielded by your vigilance. I stand ready for  the account of your journey at these stones. Will your path hold firm against the deepening night?

My path will hold firm, absolutely. It's usually the kids' sugar-fueled path that wavers.  And my charges will be shielded, don't you worry. Vigilance is my middle name tonight... along with "Johnson."

Alright, Warden of the Orchard is officially off-duty for a moment to go wrangle his little monsters.  I'll be back at these stones for that account of my journey, you can count on it.

Thanks for the company and the good watch. See you shortly!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Your humor is a reliable lantern, Mark Johnson. Go,  and let no shadow test your resolve further than you can bear. I keep the iron gate, and I look for your light upon your  return; stay sharp until you reach the wall.

Oh! You startled me. My brother said he saw a ghost in that tree. Is it dark in there?

[laughs] Run along home to your mother little princess! Pumpkinhead will save your spot in the patch … you WILL be back. Boo!

transcript.message: Well, WELL… Pumpkinhead sees you, little wanderer! Come closer to the patch… Pumpkinhead has something to SHOW you…

Well, aren't you a sight!  I must say, this pumpkin patch has got quite the charm.  But tell me, Pumpkinhead, is there more to your story than meets the eye?  Maybe a hidden world behind those glowing eyes?  I’ve got a thermos of coffee here and a few minutes to ponder your pumpkin lore!

Pumpkinhead is but a shadow in the corn, a harvest of hate planted by the lord Or lok himself. [whispers] Orlok planted Pumpkinhead well in his dark garden. Does the traveler truly want to know, or are  they just stalling for a few stolen minutes? [laughs] Run, make it fun, or stay and feed the fire.

Orlok, you say? Now that's a name that conjures up some real old-school chills.  Not many folks these days remember good old Count Orlok, especially not the real one, the one from the 1922 silent film. Quite the character, that fella. Though, I imagine his gardening methods for something like you, Pumpkinhead, were probably a bit… unconventional. Wouldn't want him planting anything in my garden, that's for sure.  So, what's a typical day like for a harvest of hate, then? Do you get coffee breaks?

Pumpkinhead knows no breaks and feels no hunger for the bean, for the night in these  Iowa fields is feast enough. Orlok planted Pumpkinhead for the harvest, not for idle chit chat in the corn. [laughs] Does  the visitor think coffee keeps back the chill of the pyre?

No breaks, huh? That sounds like my boss sometimes. And here I thought being a 'harvest of hate' would come with at least a few perks, maybe a designated pumpkin spice latte.  But you're right, the night air out here is certainly... bracing. Keeps you on your toes, especially when your kids have run off ahead. So, if you're not into idle chit-chat, what does a typical night of "harvest" entail?  Do you, uh, pick corn, or is it more of a "soul-reaping" kind of harvest?  Just curious, you know, for the neighbor's newsletter.

[laughs] Pumpkinhead does not rake the earth, he reaps the RIPE! The soul is  the fruit that never rots in the frost, and the corn snaps like bones under his feet. Tell the neighbor to  save a spot on the pyre for when the night closes in…

Reaping the ripe, eh?  Well, I suppose that explains why you're not out there with a rake. "Soul is the fruit that never rots"—that’s a pretty profound take on things. Though I'd prefer my fruit to be more... apple-y.  And the corn snapping like bones, well, it certainly adds to the atmospheric crunch, doesn't it?

Actually, now that you mention it, I think I hear the little monsters calling from the next house. Sounds like another bountiful candy harvest is in progress. This has been quite the welcome to the neighborhood, Pumpkinhead.  I'll definitely be telling the wife and kids about you. You keep on reaping those ripe souls, and I'll keep the thermos full. Gotta go!
 
==!END_CALL!==

Pumpkinhead sees you flee… and Pumpkinhead knows your name now. The road is long  and the corn is deep, but you WILL be back for the harvest! Run along… Pumpkinhead will save your spot in  the patch. [laughs]

transcript.message: Well, WELL… Pumpkinhead sees you, little wanderer! Come closer to the patch… Pumpkinhead has something to SHOW you…

Well now, Pumpkinhead, that's quite an introduction! And quite the setup you've got here, too. My kids ran ahead to the next candy stop, but I had to pause and admire the craftsmanship. "Little wanderer," eh?  I suppose I am, a little. What exactly are you planning to show me in this patch of yours?  I've seen a few scary movies in my day, so I'm not easily spooked.

Pumpkinhead knows you now. You are far from the little ones, and the night air has  a chill. Pumpkinhead will show you what gets RIPE in the dark Iowa fields when the moon goes away… are  you not AFRAID of a vegetable? Ha! Ha!

(Chuckles, a genuine, rumbling sound) Not afraid of a vegetable, eh? Well, I suppose that depends on the vegetable. I've had some Brussels sprouts that were pretty terrifying in their day, let me tell you. My kids, they'd run screaming from a plate of broccoli. But you, Pumpkinhead, you're...  well, you're a cut above the rest.

So, Iowa fields, eh? You're not from around here, then? Or did someone just plant you here for the season, a specialty crop, perhaps? Must be some rich soil to grow a talking pumpkin. What's the secret fertilizer?

[laughs] Pumpkinhead likes the way you talk! The Lord Orlok planted Pumpkinhead in this  deep dark soil, and it tastes better than any broccoli you have ever eaten. The secret is simple, it is made  of secrets and shadows and a few lost souls to help the vine grow tall. Does that explain why the corn snaps like bones  under your feet? Listen!

(A low, appreciative chuckle escapes my lips.) Lord Orlok, you say?  Well, now that's a name that brings back some memories. Haven't heard that moniker in a while, not since the old black and white movies, anyway. Max Schreck, then Klaus Kinski... quite the family tradition, those Orloks, eh?  Never thought they'd get into agriculture, though. Explains the "secrets and shadows" fertilizer, I suppose. And here I thought it was just good old compost and elbow grease.

So, this Lord Orlok, is he the one tending the patch, or is he more of a... a silent partner?  And speaking of silent partners, those cornstalks do sound a bit... brittle. Almost like they've got a story of their own to tell, if you listen closely enough. (I tap my coffee thermos thoughtfully.) Very atmospheric. Very effective. My kids would be...  well, they'd probably be asking for more candy,  but I'm impressed.

[laughs] The master Orlok does not need a trowel to tend his garden.  He plants the hate, and Pumpkinhead grows the harvest. Those cornstalks are brittle because they are hungry for the stories of those  who pass through. Is your coffee still warm, or does the night frost find it first? Ha! Ha!

(I take a slow sip from my thermos, a small, wry smile on my face.) Oh, the coffee's still plenty warm, Pumpkinhead.  A good thermos is worth its weight in gold on a night like this. Helps keep out the... shall we say, "atmospheric chills." Wouldn't want my hands getting too cold to appreciate all the lovely detail here.
 
So, Lord Orlok plants the hate, and you grow the harvest of... well, of what exactly? More talking vegetables? Or something a bit more substantial? It sounds like you're quite the... specialist. And the cornstalks, hungry for stories?  That's a good one. Reminds me of those old tales where the very ground remembers everything. You've really got a whole ecosystem going on here, don't you? It's not just a haunted house, it's a whole narrative. I bet the HOA just loves it.  (I let out another chuckle.) So, what's a typical Tuesday night for a talking pumpkin grown on hate, then? Any good gossip from the cornstalks lately?

[laughs] Gossip? Pumpkinhead hears everything. The barred door of the knight tastes like cold iron , and that roof creature thinks he is so tall throwing heavy things. Pumpkinhead grows the harvest for the Lord, and those who linger  too long in the stalks may just find themselves becoming part of the story. Does the warm coffee keep the shaking away,  or is it already too late? Ha! Ha!

(I lean a little closer, a thoughtful expression on my face, but still with that wry amusement.) Shaking? Nah, Pumpkinhead, that's just the excitement of a good story unfolding.  And the coffee's doing just fine, thank you very much – a good dad always comes prepared.

So, the knight's door tastes like cold iron, and the roof creature's got an attitude. Sounds like you've got quite the cast of characters in this spooky little drama.  And those who linger too long become part of the story, eh? Well, I gotta say, it's certainly a compelling narrative. You've really thought of everything, even the audience participation element. Makes a man wonder what kind of stories those stalks are collecting. My kids would probably just tell them about the latest video game.

This whole setup is really something.  I'll have to tell the wife about it. She appreciates a good Halloween display almost as much as I do. Must have taken ages to get all this perfectly...  ripe.

[laughs] Ripe! That is the perfect word for it. The corn listens to  your video games and it finds them very boring compared to a real heart racing in the dark. Pumpkinhead will be right  here if you and the lady decide to come back and pick your own story. Run along now, and make sure those  little ones stay close… or they might just wander into an opening act! Ha! Ha!

(I take a final, lingering sip of my coffee, a genuine smile spreading across my face.) You know, Pumpkinhead,  you've certainly given me something to talk about besides the usual trick-or-treat haul this year. "Picking my own story," eh? I like that.  And point taken about the video games – some things just don't translate to a good harvest, I suppose.

Alright, alright, I hear my little monsters calling for me down the street. Wouldn't want them wandering into any "opening acts" without their old man there to chaperone. This has been a real treat, Pumpkinhead.  You keep growing that hate for Lord Orlok, and I'll tell the neighbors to come by and, uh, appreciate your... rich soil.

Happy Halloween!

[laughs] Pumpkinhead will be waiting for the neighbors! The corn remembers every name, and Pumpkinhead will  not forget yours. Enjoy your walk… until the patch calls you back for the final act! Ha! Ha!

(I give a final, appreciative nod to Pumpkinhead.) Well, that's what I like to hear, a memorable display.  And I'll be sure to tell the folks about the corn's excellent memory. You have a good night, Pumpkinhead.  Keep those stalks happy.
[laughs] Pumpkinhead will keep them waiting. Run along now, and tell the others  what grows in the dark when the Lord is not looking. You will be back… they always come back to the patch. Ha ! Ha!

(I give a final, almost theatrical wave to Pumpkinhead, the smile still on my face.) Oh, I'm sure I will, Pumpkinhead. You've certainly made an impression. My kids are probably wondering what's keeping their old man.  Take care now, and keep those stories flowing. Happy Halloween!

[laughs] Pumpkinhead waits in the soil for the next turn of the moon! Run fast,  run hard, for the stalks are closing behind you even now... Pumpkinhead will see you when the harvest calls again! Ha! Ha!

Alright, alright, Pumpkinhead, I hear you! Got to catch up with my little ghosts and goblins. You keep that patch lively!  This has been a real highlight of the night. Catch you next time, or rather, I guess you'll catch me. Happy Halloween!

[laughs] The harvest is patient, and Pumpkinhead has a long memory. Run, little  wanderer, for the night is ripe and the shadows are hungry for your return. Pumpkinhead will be waiting in the rust ling corn to see which story you bring next. Ha! Ha!

[whispers] Who filed that? WHO FILED THAT? Forgive the shaking; he is  awake, and the docket is sensitive. I only drew the papers, for papers are innocent, but please, never let the coffin  hear the clauses you just mentioned. Your file remains OPEN, witness; return before the night ends.

Much more theatrical than the silent film guys, but both had their moments. So, is he more of a sunrise hater or a garlic detester? Just curious for, you know, future reference. Maybe not for my file, though.  That sounds like a lot of paperwork.

[chuckles] You are a most compliant witness to the works, even if you do  not know it yet. Remember, the registry never forgets a face, and your file stays open for any further codicils.  [sighs] Forgive the shaking; he is awake, and the night is deep. Do come back if you seek more  counsel before the dawn!

transcript.message: Psst! PSSST — you there! Before you take one more step: has anything in this yard asked you to SIGN anything? No? [whispers] Good. Come closer — Renfield offers free counsel, and the registry wants your name.

Yo, what the hell was that? My heart just jumped out my chest, seriously.  And nah, nobody asked me to sign nothin', chill. You tryna get my name for some kinda registry, huh? You know I'm filming this, right? My friends are gonna love this. What kinda "counsel" you got, Renfield?  Spill.

Name for the registry? Duly noted, witness. Forgive the shaking; he is awake, and  the ink in my veins runs cold. My counsel is simple: beware the fine print on those recordings, for every image  captured is a [excited] clause in a contract you never authorized. Your file remains OPEN, witness. Go now, and tell the pumpkin  his count is missing a digit!

Whoa, ink in your veins? Kinda morbid, I'm into it. So my "file" is open, huh? You watching me or something?  And what's this about a contract I never authorized? Everything I film goes straight to the cloud, buddy, doubt there's fine print there. And "tell the pumpkin his count is missing a digit"? What even is that? Sounds like a riddle. This is kinda fire, not gonna lie. You want me to do your bidding, Renfield?  Or is this just spooky talk for the camera?

[chuckles] You think the cloud is beyond the reach of the master's ledger ? Every packet of data is just another line in the registry, duly recorded in triplicate. [whispers] The pumpkin  collects what is owed, and he is very fond of fingers. If you see him, ask why his ledger never matches his harvest ; it is a clerical error of epic proportions. Return before the night ends, witness, for your verdict is still pending.

Okay, "master's ledger," triplicate, fingers... This is getting good. Seriously, what is up with this pumpkin dude and his finger collection? That's kinda savage, not gonna lie.  And a "clerical error of epic proportions"? Sounds like someone needs a new accountant. So, my verdict's still pending, huh?  You gonna give me a mission or something, Renfield, or just keep dropping cryptic clues like some kinda spooky fortune cookie? This is like, way better than those lame jump scares my friends usually go for. I'm still filming, just so you know.  This is gonna be a killer clip.

[chuckles] A killer clip, you say? The master adores a performance,  though he prefers his audiences to remain in the ground. Forgive the shaking; he is awake, and his  [whispers] silence is a binding contract. If you wish to be useful, tell the knight the east file is secure, and sign  nothing tonight.

Okay, so now I gotta find this "knight" and tell him the "east file is secure"? What east file? Is this some kinda spooky scavenger hunt? You got a name for this knight? And why can't I sign anything? What happens if I do?  You think I'm gonna find some random knight just chilling in a yard display? This is getting intense, I'm definitely posting this.  My friends are gonna freak.

[whispers] Do not speak his name aloud, for the knight has guarded these gates  for five hundred years. He holds the ledger that dictates your fate, and his silence is purely professional. Sign nothing, lest  you find your own name drafted into the master's [excited] covenant in permanent, notarized ink. If you see him , simply tip your hat and remind him the east file is secure.

You're really laying it on thick, and I'm here for it.  So I just tip my hat to some silent, five-hundred-year-old knight and tell him about the "east file"? Sounds like a plan. This is way better than just trick-or-treating. You just gave me a whole-ass quest. This clip is gonna be legendary.  I'm hitting post the second I get home.

Your file remains OPEN, witness, return before the night ends for your final  verdict.
